An AI agent followed the rules.
MetaMask can limit what an agent is allowed to do.
But staying within those limits doesn't always mean the agent understood what you wanted.
So when an agent gets the intention wrong... who decides what happens next?
Meet Internet Court: an application designed to evaluate disputes over what an AI agent was supposed to do.
GenLayer powers the AI jury behind the adjudication process.
The evidence is evaluated, and the jury works toward a decision.
Once the decision is finalized, it can have a real consequence:
the agent's permission can be revoked, preventing further payments under that delegation.
As AI agents take on more responsibility, permissions alone won't answer every difficult question.
We also need ways to evaluate their decisions when intentions and outcomes don't line up.
